**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant:** Wheat/cereal grass with upright stems and elongated leaves
- **Affected parts:** Leaves (primary), visible across most of the plant
- **Key symptoms:**
  - Numerous small, discrete **white to tan/cream-colored spots or pustules** scattered across the leaf surface
  - Spots appear **rounded to oval**, fairly uniform in size
  - Background leaf tissue shows **yellowing/chlorosis** around and between lesions
  - Some leaves showing **necrotic (orange-brown) areas**, particularly at tips/edges
  - Lesions appear to be **on the leaf surface** (not in stripes, not elongated streaks)
  - No distinct yellow stripe pattern (rules out Stripe Rust)
  - No large elongated rust pustules (rules out Stem Rust)
  - Spots are whitish/pale, not orange-brown urediniospore masses

**Differential reasoning:**

- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery colonies, typically fluffy/cottony patches — these spots are more discrete and sunken, not cottony
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Irregular tan/brown lesions with pycnidia (small black dots inside lesions), often water-soaked margins — possible, but lesions here appear rounder
- **Tan Spot**: Tan/brown lesions with yellow halo, often diamond-shaped — the yellowing halos and tan centers match well
- **Wheat Leaf Rust**: Orange-brown urediospore pustules, more raised/erupted — color doesn't match these pale spots
- **Stripe Rust**: Yellow pustules in stripes along veins — not present here

The discrete **tan/cream spots with surrounding yellow chlorotic halos** on wheat leaves, without a striped pattern and without orange rust pustules, most strongly match **Tan Spot** (*Pyrenophora tritici-repentis*). The lesions show the characteristic tan centers with yellowing halos scattered across the leaf blade.
